title: Coroutines, UniTask and cancellation
sub: What to pick in Unity and how not to outlive your object
cards/0/body:
A coroutine is a method with IEnumerator and yield return. Unity advances it every frame. It lives as long as its MonoBehaviour: destroy the object, and the coroutine stops.

But a coroutine can't return a value, and it's bad at handling exceptions.
cards/1/body: An async method knows nothing about a GameObject's lifetime. Destroy the object, or exit Play Mode in the editor, and the method keeps running. A second later it touches a destroyed transform.
cards/2/q: The object is destroyed during await Awaitable.WaitForSecondsAsync(5). What happens to an async method with no cancellation token?
cards/2/options/0: It keeps running and most likely fails when it touches the destroyed object
cards/2/explain: You have to cancel explicitly, with a token.
cards/3/body: Since Unity 2022.2, every MonoBehaviour has a destroyCancellationToken that is canceled when the object is destroyed.
cards/4/q: Stop the patrol along with the object
cards/5/body: UniTask (Cysharp) is a popular library: an allocation-free struct task, waiting on Unity frames and events, and convenient cancellation. People used it before Awaitable existed, and still use it today for its rich API.
cards/6/q: Match each tool to what it is
cards/6/pairs/0/1: IEnumerator and yield; dies with the object
cards/6/pairs/3/1: Cancellation when the object is destroyed
cards/7/q: Which are true? Select all that apply.
cards/7/options/0: A coroutine stops when its MonoBehaviour is destroyed
cards/7/options/1: An async method stops by itself when the object is destroyed
cards/7/options/3: A coroutine makes it easy to return a value
cards/7/explain: You have to cancel async yourself, and a coroutine doesn't return a value.
cards/8/q: You need to load data from a server and return the result to the game. What's more convenient?
cards/8/options/0: async Awaitable<T> or UniTask<T> with a cancellation token
cards/8/options/1: A coroutine with a global variable
cards/8/explain: Results, exceptions and cancellation come out of the box.
